header.running_head: Abstention from using Public Funds for Personal use and for Close Relatives

blocks.text: The Incident of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA)

Hadhrat Ibraheem reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to engage in trade when he was Khalifah. When he once prepared a caravan to send to Shaam, he sent someone to arrange a loan of four thousand Dirhams for him from Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA). Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) sent a message back with the messenger that Hadhrat Umar (RA) should take the loan from the public treasury and pay it back later. When the message reached him, Hadhrat Umar (RA) felt it most difficult to do so. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) met Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), he asked him, "Are you the one who said that I should take the money from the public treasury? Had I died before the caravan returns, you would say, 'The Ameerul Mu'mineen had taken the money. Let us waive it.' I shall then be taken to task for it on the Day of Qiyaamah. I shall never do such a thing. I prefer to rather take the money from a man who is as greedy and stingy as you are so that he would ensure that he takes it from my estate if I die."[^1]
The Incident of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and the Honey from the public treasury

One of the sons of Hadhrat Baraa bin Ma'roor reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once fell ill and honey was prescribed to treat him. At that time there was a vial of honey in the public treasury. Hadhrat Umar (RA) therefore came out and mounted the pulpit saying (to the people), "I shall use the honey in the public treasury only if you people permit. Otherwise it will be Haraam for me." The people gladly gave their permission.[^2]
The Incident Between Hadhrat Umar (RA) and his Daughter Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) Concerning Public Funds

Hadhrat Hasan narrates that some money once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA). When his daughter Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) heard about it, she approached him saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Relatives also have a right to that money because Allaah has advised kind treatment of relatives." He responded by saying, "Dear daughter! My relatives have a right only in my personal wealth. As for this, it is the spoils of the Muslims. Do you wish to deceive your father? Please leave." She then left, dragging her dress along.[^3]
